adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a legitimate architectural concern. The diff shows that Group model now stores pagination state (offset, limit, user_count, members) directly on the model instance (lines 27-35 in group.js). The diff also shows two different consumers: the admin group editor (admin-group.js.es6) and the public group members view (group-members.js.es6), both calling model.findMembers(). While currently both use the same Group model instance for their respective contexts, the concern about shared state is valid - if the same Group instance were ever accessed by both views, they would overwrite each other's pagination state. This is a reasonable scope/architecture concern about the design choice, though not an immediate bug since the current code paths appear to use separate model instances.
